question: In Grade 12 Physical Sciences, what is the precise CAPS definition of **'Doppler Effect'**?
correct_answer: The change in frequency (or pitch) of the sound or wave detected by a listener because the sound source and the listener have different velocities relative to the medium of sound propagation.
wrong_answers_pool: The reflection of sound waves from a solid barrier causing an acoustic echo
The change in propagation speed of sound when passing from air into water
The destructive interference of two sound waves of identical amplitude and frequency
The bending of acoustic waves around physical obstacles via diffraction
The continuous amplification of sound by an acoustic resonance chamber
The absorption of sound wave energy by soft fibrous materials
explanation: In CAPS Grade 12 Physical Sciences, the Doppler effect is strictly defined as the change in frequency (or pitch) of the sound detected by a listener because the sound source and listener have different velocities relative to the medium.

question: In Grade 12 Physical Sciences, what is the precise CAPS definition of **'Red Shift (in Astronomy)'**?
correct_answer: The shift of spectral absorption lines towards longer wavelengths (lower frequencies) in the light received from distant stars and galaxies, demonstrating that they are moving away from Earth and that the universe is expanding.
wrong_answers_pool: The shift of spectral lines towards higher frequencies as celestial bodies approach Earth
The absorption of blue and ultraviolet light by cold interstellar cosmic dust
The gradual thermodynamic cooling of an aging red giant star
The refraction and chromatic dispersion of starlight passing through the atmosphere
The emission of high-energy infrared radiation from black hole accretion disks
The Doppler broadening of spectral lines inside a stationary stellar core
explanation: Red shift occurs when a light source recedes from the observer; observed wavelength increases (shifts toward the red end of the spectrum), providing empirical evidence for the expanding universe.

tags.learning_outcome: Define Red Shift (in Astronomy)

question: In Grade 12 Physical Sciences, what is the precise CAPS definition of **'Blue Shift (in Astronomy)'**?
correct_answer: The shift of spectral absorption lines towards shorter wavelengths (higher frequencies) in the light received from a celestial object, demonstrating that the object is moving toward Earth (the observer).
wrong_answers_pool: The shift of spectral lines towards longer wavelengths indicating cosmic recession
The reflection of solar radiation from planetary liquid oceans
The Rayleigh scattering of high-frequency blue sunlight by atmospheric nitrogen
The thermal radiation peak of an extremely hot blue supergiant star
The complete polarization of starlight by interstellar galactic magnetic fields
The decrease in light frequency caused by gravitational time dilation alone
explanation: Blue shift occurs when a light source moves towards an observer; the detected wavefronts are compressed, shifting lines toward higher frequencies (the blue end).

tags.learning_outcome: Define Blue Shift (in Astronomy)

question: In Grade 12 Physical Sciences, what is the precise CAPS definition of **'Doppler Flow Meter (Ultrasound)'**?
correct_answer: A medical diagnostic instrument that uses high-frequency ultrasound waves and the Doppler effect to measure the velocity and direction of blood flow in arteries and veins.
wrong_answers_pool: A mechanical gauge that measures arterial blood pressure using an inflatable cuff
An instrument that records microvolt electrical signals produced by cardiac muscle (ECG)
An imaging apparatus that utilizes ionizing X-ray radiation to inspect bone fractures
A medical device that measures percentage oxygen saturation in peripheral capillaries
A thermal sensor that tracks fluctuations in core human body temperature
An endoscope that uses fiber optic cables to inspect gastric mucosa visually
explanation: A Doppler flow meter bounces ultrasound off moving red blood cells; the frequency shift of the reflected wave determines blood velocity.

wrong_answers_pool: Yes, the speed of sound increases by adding the speed of the source (v + v_s).

Yes, sound travels at supersonic speed whenever the source is in motion.
Yes, the speed of sound doubles whenever the frequency doubles.
Yes, the speed of sound drops to zero behind a moving sound source.
No, because sound waves cannot travel through moving atmospheric air.
explanation: No, the speed of sound depends exclusively on the physical properties of the medium (air temperature and density), NOT on the velocity of the source or listener.

wrong_answers_pool: The listener hears a frequency LOWER than 350 Hz (a lower pitch).
The listener hears a frequency that continuously rises and falls every second.
The listener hears exactly 350 Hz because vehicle motion cannot alter frequency.
The listener hears a frequency that drops to 0 Hz as distance decreases.
The listener hears double the speed of sound with identical pitch 350 Hz.
The listener hears a frequency that increases exponentially to infinity.
explanation: As the passenger train approaches at constant velocity, wavefronts are compressed in front of it. The listener detects a constant frequency higher than 350 Hz.

tags.subject: Physical Sciences
tags.learning_outcome: Explain frequency change for approaching passenger train

question: A passenger train emitting a locomotive horn of frequency 350 Hz moves directly AWAY from a stationary listener at constant speed. What pitch and frequency are detected by the listener?

The listener detects exactly 350 Hz because the vehicle has already passed.
The listener detects a frequency that fluctuates wildly between 0 Hz and 700 Hz.
The listener detects a sound wave with a compressed, shorter wavelength.
The listener detects a sound wave whose speed through the air is halved.
The listener detects ultrasonic radiation above 20 000 Hz.
